title: ChatGPT could soon let you lock chats behind a PIN or fingerprint
summary: Fixing Temporary Chat's biggest drawback.
body: TL;DR OpenAI has been spotted working on a new feature that would let you lock your chats. Locked chats could let you hide saved ChatGPT conversations from your sidebar, history, and search results behind a PIN or fingerprint. Unlike Temporary Chats, locked chats are designed to stick around, giving users a way to save sensitive conversations without leaving them visible in their regular history. Locked chats could also create a privacy boundary for Memory, letting new information from locked conversations personalize other locked chats without spilling into regular conversations. Your ChatGPT history isn’t necessarily a record that you want to parade around. From the simple math problems that don’t require AI, to asking ChatGPT to craft an email calling in sick for a day off, and from more serious conversations about private projects, to chats about finances, there are plenty of conversations you might want to keep out of others’ line of sight. With what OpenAI has been spotted developing, keeping these chats away from prying eyes could soon become a lot easier. title: The best PS3 emulator on Android just got online play
summary: We've also got a host of compatibility improvements affecting a variety of games.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR ARMSX3 has received several updates in the last few days, bringing support for online play, the ability to import save data, and more. We also get plenty of compatibility improvements, with an entire class of games now booting up. ARMSX3 is the latest PS3 emulator on Android, following in the footsteps of aPS3e and RPCSX-UI Android. Development has proceeded at a breakneck pace, and the last few updates have brought some major additions. ARMSX3 v0.9.3 was released on GitHub yesterday and brings support for online play in PS3 games. This uses the open-source RPCN framework for matchmaking in lieu of the PlayStation Network. The developer notes that your RPCN password is stored in plain text in a YML file, as is the case with RPCS3 on desktop. They therefore caution people not to reuse passwords from other services for their RPCN credentials. The update also lets you save and switch between servers.

title: TSMC could start mass producing 1.6nm chips as soon as late 2026
summary: TSMC may have already gone beyond 2nm.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR TSMC has reportedly developed a 1.6nm chip manufacturing process. The process is said to deliver an 8% to 10% increase in computing speed, and a 15% to 20% decrease in energy consumption. TSMC is expected to start mass production in Q4 2026. While everyone’s excited about 2nm chips, IBM recently blew past that limit, showing off its sub-nm architecture . As a result, TSMC and other chip makers are now left playing a game of catch-up. However, IBM estimates that it will take five years before this design is ready for production. As the company works towards that goal, TSMC is hot on IBM’s heels with a sub-2nm manufacturing process that could be ready for mass production soon. A report from Liberty Times (via Chosun ) claims that TSMC has finished the development and verification of its angstrom-class A16 (1.6nm) process. TSMC will reportedly enter the mass production phase in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: We tested the Pixel 11’s Tensor G6 chip, and the results are brutal
summary: The G6 is better, but not in the ways it needs to be.
body: I’ll be frank, my hopes for the Tensor G6 were mixed coming into the launch of the Pixel 11 series . Google has made meaningful upgrades to the CPU and TPU for traditional app and AI workloads, respectively, while switching to what should be a more efficient modem. But pairing the Pixel 11 Pro with just 12GB of RAM , down from 16GB last year, undermines its high-end AI credentials. Meanwhile, Google has dropped a CPU core from its configuration, reducing the benefits of its more modern architecture. While we can’t blame Google for the current state of the global RAM supply chain, its decision to switch to yet another mid-range graphics chip is harder to defend. Still, now that we have the phone in hand (and managed to get around Google blocking benchmarks via the Play Store), we’ve been able to run our usual suite of benchmarks to get a feel for where the Pixel 11 series falls in the performance pecking order.

title: Android 17’s new distraction-killer is a Pixel 11 exclusive, Google confirms

A recently updated support page confirms the feature’s limited availability. While Google does not outright deny the possibility of bringing it to older phones, there’s no certainty yet. It’s often one of those “you vs. you” scenarios when you move to open an app, such as TikTok or Instagram, even without intending to. The realization may not always seep in until several minutes after you’ve used the app, and by then you get caught in a vicious loop of self-loathing and the inability to quit at once. It’s safe to presume it’s the same for (almost) all mere mortals, including me, who need external checks to stop us from opening the app in the first place. And Google may have a trick just for that. With Android 17, Google introduced a new Digital Wellbeing feature to prevent “distracting” apps from hogging all your attention. This new feature, called Pause Point , lets you pause for 10 seconds and deliberate whether you really want to open one of the apps you’ve designated as distracting.
